From 10d570284258a30dc104c50787c5289ec49f3d23 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Sven Eckelmann <sven.eckelmann@openmesh.com>
Date: Mon, 19 Feb 2018 14:08:52 +0100
Subject: [PATCH] batman-adv: Ignore invalid batadv_iv_gw during netlink send

The function batadv_iv_gw_dump stops the processing loop when
batadv_iv_gw_dump_entry returns a non-0 return code. This should only
happen when the buffer is full. Otherwise, an empty message may be
returned by batadv_gw_dump. This empty message will then stop the netlink
dumping of gateway entries. At worst, not a single entry is returned to
userspace even when plenty of possible gateways exist.

Fixes: efb766af06e3 ("batman-adv: add B.A.T.M.A.N. IV bat_gw_dump implementations")
Signed-off-by: Sven Eckelmann <sven.eckelmann@openmesh.com>
Signed-off-by: Simon Wunderlich <sw@simonwunderlich.de>

diff --git a/net/batman-adv/bat_iv_ogm.c b/net/batman-adv/bat_iv_ogm.c
index 79e326383726..8f64439647e3 100644
--- a/net/batman-adv/bat_iv_ogm.c
+++ b/net/batman-adv/bat_iv_ogm.c
@@ -2729,7 +2729,7 @@ static int batadv_iv_gw_dump_entry(struct sk_buff *msg, u32 portid, u32 seq,
 	struct batadv_neigh_ifinfo *router_ifinfo = NULL;
 	struct batadv_neigh_node *router;
 	struct batadv_gw_node *curr_gw;
-	int ret = -EINVAL;
+	int ret = 0;
 	void *hdr;
 
 	router = batadv_orig_router_get(gw_node->orig_node, BATADV_IF_DEFAULT);
-- 
2.25.1

### Modifications in Each File

1. **File: `net/batman-adv/bat_iv_ogm.c`**
   - The variable `ret` was changed from being initialized to `-EINVAL` to `0`. This modification alters the behavior of the function `batadv_iv_gw_dump_entry`, allowing it to continue processing even when it encounters conditions that would previously have resulted in an error code.

### Relationships Between Modifications

- The change in the initialization of the `ret` variable directly impacts the control flow of the `batadv_iv_gw_dump` function. By setting `ret` to `0`, the function will no longer stop processing when it encounters an invalid gateway entry, thus preventing the premature termination of the netlink dumping process. This ensures that even if some entries are invalid, valid gateway entries can still be sent to userspace, addressing the issue of potentially returning no entries when there are valid gateways available.

You are a programming expert.

The code statements that lead to the bug are:
```c
-	int ret = -EINVAL;
```
```c
if (batadv_iv_gw_dump_entry returns a non-zero return code)
```
```c
goto out;
```
Reason:
The initialization of the `ret` variable to `-EINVAL` causes the function to incorrectly signal an error when it encounters conditions that should not halt processing. This leads to the premature termination of the netlink dumping process, resulting in an empty message being sent to userspace, even when valid gateway entries exist.

The code statements that fix the bug are:
```c
+	int ret = 0;
```
```c
ret = 0;
```
Reason:
By initializing `ret` to `0`, the function now correctly indicates success under normal conditions. This change ensures that the processing loop continues even when `batadv_iv_gw_dump_entry` encounters non-error conditions, allowing valid gateway entries to be sent to userspace instead of prematurely stopping the netlink dumping process.
